situation: A friend owes you three thousand rupees from a trip two months ago.
say: Bro, no pressure, but if possible, whenever you get time, that small amount...
better: Hey, can you send the three thousand from the Goa trip this week? I'm settling my accounts.
also: Just a reminder about the three thousand. Can you UPI it by Friday?
weak: Some people don't return money, I'm just saying.
Forget it, I'll never lend you anything again.
why: Name the amount and a date. Vague hints are easy to ignore.

situation: Friends plan an expensive dinner and you can't afford it this month.
say: Guys, actually I have some work, I'll not be able to come, sorry.
better: That place is out of my budget this month. Can we do the dhaba near college instead? I'm in for that.
also: I'll skip dinner but join you for dessert after.
weak: You rich people only go to fancy places.
Okay, I'll come. (and borrows money)
why: Being honest about money is normal. Suggest something you can do.

situation: A friend tells you their father is in hospital.
say: Oh no, don't worry, everything will be fine, be positive.
better: I'm so sorry. That sounds really scary. Do you want me to come to the hospital or bring you food?
also: I'm here. Call me anytime tonight, even late.
weak: My uncle also had the same thing, he was in ICU for a month...
Take care bro. 👍
why: Name the feeling and offer a specific help. Don't promise what you can't know.

situation: Your friend keeps cancelling plans at the last minute.
say: Haan, it's fine, no problem, as usual. 🙂
better: This is the third time you've cancelled last minute, and it's frustrating. Is something going on?
also: I keep making time and then it falls through. Can we only plan when you're sure?
weak: You're so unreliable, I'm done with you.
Nothing, nothing, it's okay. (and stops calling)
why: State the pattern and how it feels, then ask. Sarcasm hides the real point.

situation: Friends tease you about your accent, and it has started to hurt.
say: Haha, very funny. (laughs along and feels bad)
better: Okay, I've laughed at this enough. The accent jokes are getting to me, so can we drop them?
also: I don't mind jokes, but not this one anymore.
weak: At least I don't look like you.
Why are all of you such jerks?
why: A calm, direct line ends teasing better than laughing along or hitting back.

situation: You forgot your best friend's birthday.
say: Sorry yaar, I was so busy, you know how my office is.
better: I completely forgot your birthday, and I feel terrible. No excuse. Let me take you out this weekend.
also: I'm really sorry I missed it. Dinner's on me on Saturday.
weak: Birthdays are just a date anyway.
You also forgot mine in 2021, remember?
why: Own it without excuses and make it up with a real plan.

situation: A friend asks your honest opinion on their startup idea, and you have doubts.
say: Superb idea bro, just go for it, it'll be a hit for sure.
better: I like that you're solving a real problem. My worry is how you'll get the first hundred customers. What's the plan?
also: One thing I'd test first is whether people will actually pay for it.
weak: This will never work, trust me.
Hmm, nice, nice.
why: Honest and kind: say what's good, then one clear concern, framed as a question.

situation: Your group can't decide on weekend plans, and the chat has gone on for hours.
say: Guys, anything is fine for me, you all decide.
better: Let's settle this: Lonavala on Saturday, leave at 7 a.m., about 1,500 each. Reply yes by tonight.
also: I'll make a poll with two options. Whatever wins by 9 p.m., we do.
weak: This group is useless, nothing ever happens.
Let's see, let's see, we'll decide later.
why: A specific proposal with a deadline moves people. 'Anything is fine' adds nothing.

situation: A friend asks you to help them move flats on your only free day.
say: Ya, ya, I'll see, I'll try to come if possible.
better: I can't do Sunday, it's my only rest day. I can come on Wednesday evening to help you pack.
also: I can't help with the move, but I'll lend you my car for the day.
weak: Hire movers, why are you asking me?
Sure! (and doesn't turn up)
why: Say no clearly and offer what you can give. 'I'll try' often means no.

situation: You feel a close friend has been distant for weeks.
say: Hmm, you've become very big now, no time for us.
better: I've missed you lately. Is everything okay? I'd love to catch up properly this week.
also: We haven't really talked in a while. Did I do something, or is life just busy?
weak: Fine, don't talk, I also have other friends.
(waits for them to text first, forever)
why: Reach out with warmth and a question, not a taunt.

situation: A friend splits a restaurant bill equally, but you only had a soup.
say: Okay, okay, no problem. (pays 1,200 for a soup)
better: Can we split by what we ordered tonight? I just had the soup, so I'll pay 250 and a share of the tip.
also: I'll pay for mine separately. Splitwise makes it easy.
weak: You all always take advantage of me.
I'm never coming out with you people again.
why: It's fair and normal to ask. Say it simply, at the table, without drama.

situation: Your friend shares something they told you in confidence with others, and you found out.
say: It's okay, whatever, I don't care anymore.
better: I told you that in confidence, and I heard you shared it. That really hurt. Why did you do it?
also: I trusted you with that. I need you to keep private things private.
weak: You're a snake, everyone should know.
I'll tell everyone your secrets now.
why: Say what happened and how it felt. Then give them a chance to explain.

situation: A friend asks you to lie to their girlfriend about where they were.
say: Bro code, done. But don't drag me in later.
better: I'm not going to lie to her for you. Whatever happened, it's better if you tell her yourself.
also: Keep me out of this one. I won't lie for you.
weak: Okay, okay, I'll say you were with me.
I'm telling her everything right now.
why: Refuses calmly without lecturing or betraying either person.

situation: Your friend just lost their job and is embarrassed to talk about it.
say: Arre, don't take tension, chill, something will come.
better: That's a hard hit. You're good at what you do. Want me to look at your CV or share it with my team?
also: Want to just get chai and not talk about it at all?
weak: Layoffs happen to bad performers, no?
I knew that company was bad, I told you.
why: Respect their feelings, then offer real, practical help.

situation: You need to say no to being a friend's guarantor for a big loan.
say: Actually, my father doesn't allow me to sign such things.
better: I can't be your guarantor. I have a rule never to sign for loans, and it's not about you.
also: I'm not comfortable with that risk, but I'll help you find other options.
weak: I don't trust you with money.
Let me think, I'll tell you next month. (and avoids them)
why: Own the no as your decision. Blaming others invites them to 'convince' your father.

situation: A friend teases you for not drinking at parties.
say: No, no, actually, I have a stomach problem, that's why.
better: I just don't drink. I'm having a great time with my nimbu soda, so don't worry about me.
also: Not for me, thanks. Pass the chakna though.
weak: Drinking is for losers anyway.
Okay, just one small one. (doesn't want to)
why: You don't need a medical excuse. A relaxed, simple no is enough.

situation: You hurt a friend with a joke at their expense in front of others.
say: Arre, I was just joking, you're too sensitive yaar.
better: I'm sorry about that joke yesterday. It wasn't funny, and I shouldn't have said it in front of everyone.
also: That came out mean. I'm sorry, it won't happen again.
weak: Sorry if you felt bad, but it was a joke.
Everyone laughed, so it was fine.
why: Apologise for what you did. Don't make their hurt the problem.

situation: A friend constantly talks about their problems and never asks about you.
say: Hmm, ya, ya, true. (silently, every week)
better: I love being there for you. Lately I've had a lot going on too, and I'd like to talk about it.
also: Can I share something that's been on my mind?
weak: You're so selfish, it's always about you.
(stops picking up their calls)
why: Ask for space in the friendship directly, without accusing them.

situation: Your friend is getting married and wants you to plan the bachelor trip, but you're swamped.
say: Bro, done, I'll handle everything, chill. (has no time at all)
better: I'd love to be part of it, but I can't plan it all this month. Can Neha lead and I'll handle the bookings?
also: I'll take care of one part, like the stay. Who can do the rest?
weak: Why me? Ask someone else.
Yes, yes, I'll do it. (and leaves it to the last day)
why: Offer what you can really do. An honest limit beats a broken promise.

situation: A friend asks if you like their new haircut, and you don't.
say: Wow, superb, looking like a hero! (doesn't mean it)
better: It's a big change! It suits your face shape. I liked the longer style too, honestly.
also: It's different. Do you like it? That's what counts.
weak: Honestly, it looks terrible.
Who cut it? Get your money back.
why: Be kind and honest at once: find something true to say.

situation: A friend keeps sending you voice notes of five minutes each.
say: Bro, I didn't hear, what did you say? Send text na.
better: I'm in office most of the day, so I often can't play voice notes. Could you text the main point?
also: Long voice notes are hard for me to catch. A quick text works better.
weak: Nobody has time for your podcasts.
(never replies to them)
why: Explain your situation and ask for what works. No mocking needed.

situation: You want to check on a friend who has seemed low and quiet lately.
say: What happened to you? Why are you so dull these days?
better: You've seemed quieter lately. I'm not prying, but if something's going on, I'm here to listen.
also: How are you really doing? You can tell me.
weak: Come on, smile, life is short!
Are you depressed or what?
why: Notice gently and open the door. Don't label or push.

situation: Your friend keeps borrowing your car and returning it with no petrol.
say: No issue, take it. (and fills petrol every time, annoyed)
better: Sure, take it. Just fill the tank back to where it was, the last few times it came back empty.
also: Happy to lend it, but please return it with petrol.
weak: Never ask for my car again.
My car is not a free taxi, okay?
why: Say yes with a clear condition. Small fixes now stop big resentment later.

situation: A friend says something sexist about women drivers in the group chat.
say: 😂😂 (and says nothing)
better: Not funny, man. My sister drives better than all of us.
also: Come on, that joke's old and unfair.
weak: You're a disgusting misogynist, I'm reporting you.
Haha, but true though. (agrees to fit in)
why: A short, light pushback works. You don't need a lecture to make the point.

situation: You want to reconnect with a school friend you haven't spoken to in years.
say: Hi. Remember me? 🙂
better: Hi Farhan! I came across our Class 10 photo and thought of you. How have you been? Would love to catch up.
also: It's been too long! Are you still in Kochi? Coffee sometime?
weak: Hi, long time. So, what's going on?
Hi bro, can you refer me in your company?
why: Give a reason you thought of them and a warm, specific opener.
